title: Graphs of Quadratic Functions
seo_title: Quadratic Graphs – SSS 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Draw and read graphs of quadratic functions; find the roots, turning point and axis of symmetry; use graphs to solve equations. (summary of the NERDC SSS 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 maths worksheets on quadratic graphs: tables of values, roots, turning points, axis of symmetry and solving equations from graphs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The roots are where the curve cuts the x-axis
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Make a table of values and plot the points with a smooth curve.
  • If a > 0 the curve has a minimum; if a < 0 it has a maximum.
  • To solve ax² + bx + c = k, draw y = k and read the x-values where it meets the curve.

Examples

Example

y = x² − 4x + 3

Roots x = 1 and 3

x = (1 + 3) ÷ 2

Answer: Turning point (2, −1)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Joining points with straight linesDraw a smooth curve.
Squaring a negative wrongly(−3)² = 9.
Reading y instead of x for rootsRoots are x-values on the x-axis.

items.q: Complete the table of values for y = x2 − 3x + 4. What is y when x = −3?
items.e: Substitute x = −3: (−3)2 − 3(−3) + 4 = 22. Remember (−3)2 = 9, not −9. 22.

items.q: What is the minimum value of y = (x − 2)2 − 1?
items.e: A square is never negative, so the least value is when (x − 2)2 = 0: y = −1.

items.q: What is the maximum value of y = −(x − 5)2 + 6, and when does it occur?
items.e: The largest value of −(x − 5)2 is 0, at x = 5. So the maximum is y = 6 when x = 5.

items.q: The graph of y = −(x − 3)2 + 9 has a maximum point. What are its coordinates?
items.e: −(x − 3)2 is never positive, so y is greatest when x = 3. The maximum point is (3, 9).
